title: THRIVE Project 2026: Transforming Women’s Economic Empowerment, Climate Resilience, and Inclusive Livelihoods in Nigeria
summary: Women continue to play a vital role in driving economic growth, strengthening families, and building resilient communities. However, many women—particularly those living in underserved communities and women with disabilities—still face significant barriers to accessing finance, markets, productive resources, and leadership opportunities. Addressing these challenges requires targeted interventions that promote gender equality, economic inclusion, and sustainable development. The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is one such initiative designed to empower women economically while transforming the systems that continue to limit their participation. Implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) as part of the Christian Aid Women Transforming Economies Signature Programme in Nigeria , THRIVE seeks to create lasting change by improving women s access to dignified work, financial opportunities, entrepreneurship support, climate-resilient livelihoods, and decision-making processes. This comprehensive 48-month initiative focuses on strengthening local economic systems so that women can thrive as entrepreneurs, farmers, business owners, and community leaders while promoting inclusive economic development. About the THRIVE Project The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is a four-year development initiative aimed at transforming local economies to become more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable for women. The project recognizes that meaningful economic empowerment goes beyond providing financial support. It also requires changing the structures, relationships, policies, and social norms that prevent women from fully participating in economic activities. Through collaboration with community stakeholders, financial institutions, women s organizations, policymakers, and development partners, THRIVE seeks to build economic systems that value women s contributions and ensure equal access to opportunities. The project is funded by Christian Aid and implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) in Nigeria. Project Duration The THRIVE project will run for: 48 months (4 years) This extended implementation period allows for sustainable interventions, long-term capacity building, and measurable improvements in women s economic participation and resilience. Geographic Focus The THRIVE project is currently being implemented in: Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area (LGA) Nasarawa State Nigeria Communities participating in the project are carefully selected through detailed assessments that consider: Gender inclusion Disability inclusion Market accessibility Community needs Economic vulnerability This approach ensures that resources reach women and communities with the greatest need. The Challenges THRIVE Seeks to Address Across many communities, women continue to face structural inequalities that prevent them from achieving economic independence. THRIVE aims to address several key challenges, including: Limited Access to Finance Many women entrepreneurs and farmers struggle to obtain: Business financing Agricultural loans Investment capital Savings opportunities Financial services Without adequate financial support, expanding businesses or increasing productivity becomes extremely difficult. Limited Access to Productive Assets Women often have fewer opportunities to access essential productive resources such as: Agricultural land Modern farming tools Equipment Technology Business infrastructure These limitations reduce income generation and long-term economic growth. Unsafe and Unequal Market Conditions Many women operate within markets that present significant barriers, including: Gender discrimination Limited market access Low bargaining power Poor infrastructure Unfair trading conditions THRIVE seeks to improve women s ability to participate in profitable and inclusive markets. Unpaid Care Responsibilities Women frequently shoulder unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities that reduce the time available for: Business development Skills training Employment Leadership Economic participation Reducing this burden is essential for achieving gender-equitable economies. Limited Participation in Decision-Making Women often have little influence over: Local economic policies Community planning Market governance Resource allocation Development priorities THRIVE supports women s participation in leadership and policy discussions that directly affect their livelihoods. Project Goal The primary goal of THRIVE is to build gender-just economies where women enjoy: Greater economic rights Increased income security Improved access to productive opportunities Equal participation in markets Stronger influence over economic policies Sustainable and resilient livelihoods Ultimately, the project seeks to transform local economic systems into environments where women can succeed without discrimination or structural barriers. APPLY HERE THRIVE s Four Strategic Pillars The project is built around four integrated intervention areas that work together to strengthen women s economic empowerment. 1. Evidence for Change THRIVE generates research and evidence on barriers affecting women to promote informed policy development. Activities include: Research on unpaid care work Studies on disability inclusion Gender analysis Policy advocacy Community consultations Evidence-based recommendations The information gathered helps shape more inclusive economic policies and practices. 2. Enterprise Development and Skills Building The project equips women with practical knowledge and business skills needed for long-term success. Support includes: MSME coaching Entrepreneurship development Business management training Digital literacy training Enterprise growth support Skills development for young women Capacity building for women with disabilities These interventions help women establish, strengthen, and expand their businesses. 3. Financial Inclusion and Market Access Access to finance and profitable markets is critical for sustainable economic growth. THRIVE strengthens women s financial opportunities by: Supporting Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) Connecting women with financial institutions Improving access to capital Facilitating market linkages Expanding business networks Strengthening value chains These efforts enable women to grow sustainable enterprises and increase household incomes. 4. Climate Resilience Climate change continues to threaten livelihoods, particularly for women working in agriculture. THRIVE promotes climate-smart economic activities including: Poultry production Apiculture (beekeeping) Dry-season gardening Climate-resilient farming Livelihood diversification Sustainable agricultural practices These initiatives help women adapt to climate change while improving food security and income generation. Who Will Benefit? The THRIVE project directly supports 300 women from various economic backgrounds. Primary beneficiaries include: Women-led Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Aspiring women entrepreneurs Women farmers Agro-processors Women with disabilities The project prioritizes women facing economic exclusion and limited access to development opportunities. Strategic Partnerships Successful implementation of THRIVE relies on collaboration with multiple stakeholders. Key partners include: Christian Aid Women Environmental Programme (WEP) Women s Rights Organisations (WROs) Local policymakers Financial institutions Community leaders Development partners These partnerships strengthen implementation while ensuring sustainable community ownership. Expected Impact Through its integrated approach, THRIVE aims to deliver long-term outcomes including: Increased economic independence for women Improved entrepreneurship capacity Greater financial inclusion Enhanced market participation Stronger climate resilience Improved policy influence Better livelihoods for women and families Inclusive local economic development Reduced gender inequality Sustainable community growth Why the THRIVE Project Matters Women s economic empowerment is one of the strongest drivers of sustainable development. When women have equal access to financial resources, education, entrepreneurship opportunities, and leadership positions, communities become more resilient, economies become stronger, and poverty declines. The THRIVE project addresses not only individual economic challenges but also the systemic barriers that prevent women from fully participating in economic life. By investing in women entrepreneurs, farmers, and women with disabilities, the project contributes to inclusive development while supporting broader goals of gender equality, climate resilience, and economic justice. Its comprehensive model demonstrates how coordinated interventions across finance, skills development, policy, and climate adaptation can create lasting and transformative change. Visit HERE to learn more about the THRIVE Project 2026 Conclusion The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project represents a significant investment in women s economic empowerment in Nigeria. Through entrepreneurship support, financial inclusion, climate-resilient livelihoods, policy advocacy, and capacity building, the project seeks to create lasting opportunities for women while transforming the local economic systems that shape their lives. By directly supporting women-led enterprises, aspiring entrepreneurs, farmers, and women with disabilities, THRIVE contributes to building more inclusive, resilient, and gender-just economies. As implementation continues over its 48-month duration, the project is expected to deliver meaningful improvements in livelihoods, economic participation, and sustainable community development across Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area. title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 for Early Career Researchers (Fully Funded to Germany)
summary: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and the British Academy have officially opened applications for the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 , a prestigious international research collaboration programme designed for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences . The symposium offers an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars from the United Kingdom and Germany to collaborate on pressing global issues surrounding the relationship between humans and nature while building long-term international research partnerships. The symposium, scheduled to take place from 21–23 April 2027 , will bring together approximately 30 outstanding early career researchers , with around 15 participants from the United Kingdom and 15 from Germany , creating an interdisciplinary platform for networking, intellectual exchange, and collaborative research. In addition to fully covering participants travel-related expenses, the programme also provides opportunities to compete for seed funding to support future international collaborative research projects. If you are an early career researcher passionate about sustainability, resilience, environmental justice, policy development, or the intersection between society and nature, this symposium presents an outstanding opportunity to connect with leading researchers and develop meaningful international collaborations. About the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 The Knowledge Frontiers Symposium is a collaborative initiative jointly organized by the British Academy and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation . The programme is specifically designed to strengthen research partnerships between scholars in the United Kingdom and Germany while encouraging interdisciplinary approaches to solving today s most complex societal and environmental challenges. The 2027 symposium will be held between: Wednesday, 21 April 2027 Friday, 23 April 2027 Before the physical symposium begins, participants will also have opportunities to engage virtually by discussing research interests, exchanging ideas, and beginning collaborative conversations that can continue during and after the event. Rather than functioning as a traditional academic conference, the symposium emphasizes interactive discussions, collaborative learning, networking, and the development of future joint research initiatives. Symposium Theme Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future The 2027 edition focuses on the broad interdisciplinary theme: Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future. The organizers recognize that the relationship between humans and the natural environment has become one of the defining issues of the modern world. Throughout history, there have been different perspectives regarding humanity s place within nature. Some viewpoints argue that humans possess the authority to manage and control nature, while others believe humans are an integral part of nature and should coexist with natural systems in more sustainable and balanced ways. Today, increasing global crises—including climate change, biodiversity loss, technological transformation, economic pressures, environmental degradation, and population growth—have intensified the urgency of reconsidering this relationship. The symposium aims to encourage participants to rethink how societies interact with ecological systems while identifying practical and innovative pathways toward greater resilience. Research Topics Participants are encouraged to explore a wide variety of interdisciplinary perspectives. Potential discussion areas include, but are not limited to: Contested understandings of society and nature Human-nature conceptualizations Environmental and social justice Sustainability challenges Ecological resilience Coupled human-natural systems Ethics and philosophy Political dimensions of environmental governance Economic approaches to sustainability Geographical perspectives Public policy development Knowledge production Narrative development Artistic perspectives on environmental challenges Interdisciplinary research approaches Future resilience strategies Researchers from diverse academic backgrounds are encouraged to contribute fresh perspectives and innovative ideas. Objectives of the Symposium The symposium has several important goals, including: Strengthening collaboration between UK and German researchers. Building long-term interdisciplinary research networks. Encouraging innovative thinking across humanities and social sciences. Promoting international academic partnerships. Supporting future collaborative research initiatives. Developing practical policy solutions for sustainability and resilience. Encouraging knowledge sharing among early career scholars. Providing networking opportunities with leading researchers. Facilitating cross-disciplinary discussions on global challenges. Symposium Format Unlike conventional academic meetings, the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium prioritizes interaction and collaboration. Participants can expect: Interactive research discussions Thematic sessions Collaborative workshops Networking activities Group debates Research idea exchanges Collaborative planning sessions Opportunities to establish future partnerships The programme allocates substantial time for participants to build professional relationships and explore opportunities for future joint projects. Seed Funding for Future Collaborations One of the most attractive features of the symposium is the opportunity to apply for seed funding . Participants will have the chance to develop collaborative research proposals during the symposium through a dedicated sandpit session held on the final day. During this session, researchers will: Form international research teams Develop collaborative project ideas Draft research proposals Submit seed funding applications before the symposium concludes Eligible collaborations may involve: Bilateral partnerships International research groups Interdisciplinary collaborations The organizers emphasize that funded collaborations must have an international composition . Benefits of the Programme Successful applicants will enjoy numerous benefits, including: Fully Funded Participation The symposium covers: Travel costs Accommodation Visa expenses Participants are therefore able to focus entirely on the academic programme without worrying about major travel-related costs. International Networking Participants will have the opportunity to: Meet leading early career researchers. Build long-lasting professional relationships. Expand international academic networks. Identify future collaborators. Research Collaboration Researchers will: Share ongoing research. Exchange innovative ideas. Learn from scholars in different disciplines. Develop interdisciplinary collaborations. Career Development The symposium supports career progression by helping participants: Increase international research visibility. Strengthen collaborative research experience. Build competitive research portfolios. Access future funding opportunities. Opportunity to Secure Seed Funding Participants may receive funding to continue collaborative research after the symposium through competitive seed funding proposals. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy the following eligibility criteria: Be an early career researcher . Be affiliated with a research institution in either the United Kingdom or Germany . Demonstrate strong research interest in the symposium theme. Show commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration. Demonstrate potential for career development through participation. Applications will be evaluated based on: Research interests Relevance to the symposium theme Commitment to interdisciplinary engagement Career development potential Application Process Interested applicants must complete an online application through the Flexi-Grant® system. Applicants are advised to carefully review the official scheme guidance before submitting their application. Incorrectly completed applications may be declared ineligible. Successful applicants are expected to: Attend the entire symposium. Travel on the designated dates determined by the organizers. Successful candidates are expected to be notified by the end of November 2026 . Late or incorrectly submitted applications will not be considered. APPLY HERE Contact Information For further enquiries regarding the symposium, applicants may contact: Email: international@thebritishacademy.ac.uk Why You Should Apply The Knowledge Frontiers Symposium is much more than an academic meeting. It provides early career researchers with a unique opportunity to: Develop international collaborations. Gain interdisciplinary research experience. Build professional networks across two leading research nations. Engage with experts tackling some of today s most urgent societal and environmental challenges. Access future collaborative funding opportunities. Advance their academic careers within an international research environment. For researchers seeking meaningful international partnerships and opportunities to contribute to global conversations on sustainability and resilience, this symposium represents an exceptional platform. Through fully funded participation, extensive networking opportunities, and access to competitive seed funding, the symposium equips emerging scholars with the resources and connections needed to advance both their research and academic careers. title: AIXI Labs Research Fellowship 2026: Fully Remote AI Safety Fellowship with Monthly Stipend of £2,000–£3,500 (Worldwide Applications Open)

title: City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship 2026: Apply for the Paid Sixalism Program in Chicago
summary: City Bureau is accepting applications for its Fall 2026 Civic Information Fellowship, a paid, six-month professional development and community engagement program designed for people interested in journalism, civic participation, storytelling, public policy and community organizing. The fellowship provides participants with practical training, individualized coaching and hands-on experience in identifying and addressing the information needs of Chicago communities. Fellows will work alongside City Bureau staff and other cohort members to research civic issues, engage with residents and create projects that help people access and use important local information. The Fall 2026 fellowship cycle is scheduled to begin on September 8, 2026. Applications must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on August 11, 2026. City Bureau has stated that late applications will not be accepted. About City Bureau City Bureau is a Chicago-based civic media laboratory that develops people-powered journalism practices and supports their adoption in communities across the United States. The organization envisions communities in which people have access to the information, resources and tools they need to make informed decisions, shape their futures and participate meaningfully in democratic and civic life. City Bureau’s work is rooted in the belief that local journalism should strengthen relationships, expand access to information, recognize community knowledge and contribute to a more equitable and participatory democracy. The organization was founded in Chicago and continues to place significant emphasis on the experiences, histories and information needs of communities across the city. About the City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship The Civic Information Fellowship is a paid, two-phase program lasting approximately six months. It is intended for Chicago-area residents who want to develop their capabilities in: Community engagement Civic participation Community-centered journalism Public-interest storytelling Research and interviewing Local government and public policy Information distribution Audience engagement Project development Professional communication With guidance from City Bureau staff, fellows will work individually and collaboratively to understand the information needs of Chicago communities. They will then design and implement projects that make useful civic information more accessible to residents. The program gives particular attention to Chicago’s South and West sides. Fellows will be expected to spend meaningful time engaging with communities, building relationships, gathering information and understanding how residents create, receive and share information. Participants will also examine how people engage with public institutions and participate in civic life. The fellowship encourages fellows to think creatively about improving local information systems, especially within Chicago’s communities of color. Purpose of the Fellowship The fellowship is not limited to conventional newsroom reporting. Its broader purpose is to help participants understand how information affects community participation, government accountability and residents’ ability to navigate important public systems. During the program, fellows will explore questions such as: What information do community members need? What prevents people from accessing reliable information? Which public systems or civic processes are difficult to understand? How can journalists and community organizations build stronger relationships with residents? What formats are most effective for sharing information with different audiences? How can information be distributed to the people who need it most? How can residents use information to make decisions or hold institutions accountable? Fellows will use their findings to design practical information-needs projects that respond to issues identified through community engagement. What Selected Fellows Will Do Participants will complete a combination of workshops, team meetings, community assignments, research activities, reflective exercises and project-development work. 1. Attend weekly workshops Fellows will participate in weekly learning sessions led by City Bureau staff members and invited speakers. These workshops will cover topics related to journalism, civic life, community engagement, storytelling and project implementation. 2. Participate in weekly team meetings Participants will meet regularly with City Bureau’s Civic Information and Engagement team. These meetings will provide opportunities to discuss assignments, review progress, address challenges and receive guidance. 3. Work collaboratively Each fellow will work in a hands-on learning environment with City Bureau staff and five other fellowship participants. Collaboration will be central to the experience. Fellows will share ideas, provide feedback, support one another’s projects and collectively examine Chicago’s information ecosystem. 4. Build journalism skills The journalism component may include training and practical experience in: Storytelling Writing for different platforms and audiences Research Information gathering Interviewing techniques Journalism ethics Accountability reporting Explainer writing Social video production Public-interest communication The program is designed to help participants communicate complex civic issues in formats that community members can understand and use. 5. Develop community-engagement skills Fellows will learn how to establish meaningful and non-transactional relationships with residents and community partners. Training and assignments may include: Community relationship-building Collaboration with local organizations Community asset mapping Conducting surveys Identifying community resources Understanding local information networks Examining how residents receive and share information City Bureau’s approach treats community engagement as a core part of journalism rather than as a temporary outreach activity. The organization emphasizes long-term relationships, shared learning and respect for the knowledge and resources that already exist within communities. 6. Strengthen civic-participation knowledge Participants will improve their understanding of how Chicago’s government and public institutions operate. This may involve: Learning how city government works Researching public policy Attending and covering public meetings Identifying responsible government officials Understanding public decision-making structures Examining government accountability Learning how residents can participate in civic processes 7. Maintain weekly journals Fellows will keep written or audio journals throughout the program. These journals will be used to document progress, reflect on lessons learned and evaluate personal and project development. 8. Produce public-facing content Participants will create content related to their fellowship work and selected civic issues. This content may include: Social media videos Blog posts Explainer articles Community information resources Project updates Stories about civic governance Content explaining public infrastructure or government systems 9. Design an information-needs project One of the fellowship’s central responsibilities will be the development of a project that addresses a community information need. Fellows will spend time engaging with residents, identifying information gaps and developing a project capable of responding to a specific issue. Projects may use different formats depending on the community need, target audience and information being communicated. 10. Develop distribution strategies Producing information will only be one part of the project. Fellows will also be expected to determine how that information can reach the people who need it. Participants will develop distribution and audience-engagement strategies to ensure that their work is accessible, relevant and actionable. The goal is to create information that people can apply in their daily lives rather than content that is simply published without a clear distribution plan. 11. Receive coaching and professional development City Bureau staff and editors will provide fellows with one-on-one feedback and additional coaching. The program will also support participants in areas such as: Career development Professional goal-setting Accountability Time management Project planning Identifying professional strengths Meeting personal and program objectives 12. Promote completed work Fellows will have opportunities to share their projects through City Bureau’s networks and community partnerships. This can help participants develop a professional portfolio, strengthen community relationships and expand the reach of their work. Fellowship Structure The City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship is divided into two phases. Each phase has different objectives, working hours and payment arrangements. Phase One: Community Research and Project Design During the first phase, fellows will focus on spending time within communities and understanding residents’ information needs. Participants will conduct research, engage with community members, map local resources and begin designing a project that responds to an identified information gap. Phase One duration Phase One will last 14 weeks. Phase One time commitment Fellows must complete approximately 12 hours of work each week. The weekly schedule will generally include: A two-hour learning session on Monday or Tuesday A four-hour in-person meeting and co-working session on Wednesday Six flexible hours for independent and community-based work Monday or Tuesday learning sessions will normally be conducted through Zoom during evening hours. City Bureau will work with selected fellows to identify a suitable meeting time. Some sessions may occasionally be held in person. Wednesday sessions will be held at City Bureau’s Bronzeville office. Fellows will attend either from noon to 4 p.m. or from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. These sessions will include meetings with City Bureau staff and co-working time with the fellowship group. Lunch will be provided. The remaining six hours may be scheduled more flexibly. Fellows will use this time for activities such as: Community engagement Research and information gathering Interviews Community mapping Writing Fellowship assignments Journaling Communication with team members Phase One stipend Participants will receive a stipend of $5,000 for completing Phase One. Payments will be issued in two-week increments. Phase One attendance requirements Required sessions are mandatory. Fellows may miss up to four required sessions during the 14-week period. Any missed time must be completed during surrounding weeks. Failure to meet the attendance and participation requirements may affect a fellow’s ability to complete the program. Phase Two: Project Implementation Fellows who successfully complete Phase One will be invited to continue into Phase Two. During this stage, participants will move from research and project design to implementation. They will carry out the information-needs projects developed during the first phase and receive continuing support from City Bureau teams. Phase Two duration Phase Two will last 10 weeks. Phase Two time commitment Participants must complete approximately eight hours of work each week. The schedule will include: One two-hour virtual learning session focused on an advanced skill One two-hour in-person co-working session with fellows and City Bureau staff Four flexible hours for implementing project activities The flexible working time may be used for completing project tasks, producing information resources, engaging with communities and receiving support from City Bureau’s Civic Information and Engagement and Chicago Documenters teams. Phase Two stipend Participants will receive a stipend of $2,800 during Phase Two. Payments will be distributed in two-week increments. Fellows who complete both phases may therefore receive a combined stipend of up to $7,800. Phase Two attendance requirements The Phase Two time commitment is mandatory. Fellows may miss up to three required sessions during the 10-week period and must make up the missed time during adjacent weeks. Important Participation Requirements Applicants do not need a particular professional qualification or a formal journalism background. City Bureau is interested in people who have demonstrated engagement with civic issues, journalism, public policy, community work or organizing. This experience may have been developed through: Personal initiatives Community projects Volunteer work Educational programs Professional training School activities Internships Journalism projects Chicago Documenters participation Direct lived experience Applicants should be interested in storytelling, community-building, civic information and finding creative ways to connect people with important information. Former City Bureau fellows are permitted to apply. Because the fellowship includes substantial in-person engagement, applicants must live in Chicago or the surrounding area. City Bureau does not offer a fully remote participation option. Participants must have reliable transportation to City Bureau’s Bronzeville office and to neighborhoods across Chicago’s South and West sides. Applicants must also be legally authorized to work in the United States. City Bureau particularly values applicants with lived or professional experience on Chicago’s South and West sides. Active and experienced Chicago Documenters are also strongly valued. The organization cautions full-time students about applying because of the program’s significant weekly workload. Exceptions may occasionally be considered for students who can demonstrate that they are capable of managing multiple time commitments effectively. Who Would Be a Strong Candidate? A strong applicant may be someone who: Regularly asks questions about how public institutions operate Cares about local civic issues Wants to improve access to community information Enjoys interviewing and listening to people Is interested in journalism or public-interest communication Has participated in community initiatives Understands issues affecting Chicago neighborhoods Wants to learn about public policy and local government Can collaborate effectively with a small team Is comfortable receiving feedback Can manage mandatory weekly commitments Is interested in designing practical community projects Values racial equity and community-centered journalism Can travel to different Chicago neighborhoods Professional journalism experience may be helpful, but it is not mandatory. City Bureau is primarily looking for applicants who demonstrate curiosity, commitment, reliability and a genuine interest in community information. Mandatory In-Person Participation Applicants should carefully consider the in-person requirements before submitting an application. The fellowship requires participants to: Attend Wednesday meetings at the Bronzeville office Travel throughout Chicago’s South and West Side neighborhoods Conduct direct community engagement Complete local interviews and assignments Participate in in-person co-working sessions Maintain regular attendance Repeated absences may place a fellow’s completion of the program at risk. Applicants should therefore confirm that their employment, education, family responsibilities and transportation arrangements will allow them to meet the required schedule. Important Policy on Artificial Intelligence City Bureau has explicitly instructed applicants not to use artificial intelligence to complete their fellowship applications. The selection team wants applicants to communicate their own ideas, experiences and perspectives. Using AI-generated content in an application may result in disqualification. Applicants should therefore write their application responses independently and ensure that the submitted material authentically reflects their personal voice, lived experience and reasons for applying. Optional Fellowship Webinar and Question-and-Answer Session City Bureau will conduct an optional online webinar and question-and-answer session on July 30, 2026, from noon to 1 p.m. The session will be held through Zoom and will provide prospective applicants with an opportunity to learn more about the fellowship and ask questions about the program or application process. Participation in the webinar is optional and is not presented as a mandatory application requirement. Interested individuals should register through the webinar registration option available on the official fellowship webpage. Application Process Applicants must complete the official online application form linked through City Bureau’s Civic Information Fellowship webpage. Before applying, candidates should: Review the complete fellowship schedule. Confirm their availability for mandatory weekly sessions. Consider whether they can complete the required weekly working hours. Confirm that they can travel to the Bronzeville office and other Chicago neighborhoods. Review the two-phase structure and attendance requirements. Prepare original responses based on their own experiences. Submit the application before the deadline. Avoid using artificial intelligence to draft or complete application answers. Applicants with questions about the fellowship expectations or application process may contact the fellowship team through the email address provided on the official program page. Application Deadline Click HERE to apply. The deadline for the City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship Fall 2026 cycle is: August 11, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Late submissions will not be accepted. The fellowship cycle is expected to begin on September 8, 2026. Applicants should submit well before the closing time to avoid technical problems or incomplete submissions. Conclusion The City Bureau Civic Information Fellowship 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for Chicago-area residents who want to develop practical skills in community engagement, civic participation, journalism and public-interest storytelling. Unlike a conventional classroom-based training program, the fellowship combines structured workshops with direct community engagement, collaborative research, professional coaching and real-world project implementation. Selected fellows will have the opportunity to identify an important community information need and develop a practical project that helps Chicago residents understand and navigate civic issues. With up to $7,800 in combined stipend support across both phases, the fellowship also enables participants to dedicate substantial time to training, community work and project development. Prospective applicants should carefully review the mandatory in-person schedule, transportation requirements, working-hour commitments and attendance rules before applying. Applications must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on August 11, 2026, and all responses must be written independently without the use of artificial intelligence. title: UNESCO World Conference on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) 2027 Call for Proposals: Submit a Parallel Session for the Global Conference in Nairobi, Kenya
summary: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has officially opened the Call for Proposals for Parallel Sessions for the UNESCO World Conference on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) 2027 , inviting organizations and institutions from around the world to contribute to one of the most significant global gatherings focused on sustainable education. Scheduled to take place in Nairobi, Kenya, from 13–15 January 2027 , the conference will bring together ministers, policymakers, educators, youth leaders, researchers, civil society organizations, United Nations agencies, private sector representatives, and other stakeholders to accelerate global action on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) . As the international community enters the final implementation phase of the ESD for 2030 Framework , the conference will serve as a strategic platform for shaping the future of education, strengthening international collaboration, and generating innovative ideas that empower learners to address today s most pressing global challenges. Organizations with expertise in sustainability, education, climate action, youth development, public policy, innovation, social inclusion, or related fields are encouraged to submit proposals to co-organize thematic parallel sessions that contribute to the conference s objectives. Hosted jointly by UNESCO and the Government of Kenya , the conference aims to create renewed momentum for the implementation of the ESD for 2030 Framework while providing strategic direction beyond 2030. The conference recognizes that education is one of the most powerful tools for addressing complex global issues such as: Climate change Biodiversity loss Environmental degradation Social inequality Poverty Conflict and peacebuilding Sustainable economic development Technological transformation Inclusive societies Participants will explore how education systems can better prepare learners of all ages with the knowledge, competencies, values, and attitudes needed to build a more sustainable future. Build resilient communities. The conference will explore how these objectives can be advanced through innovative educational approaches across different regions and contexts. Technological Innovation Participants will explore how rapid technological advancements can support sustainable education while addressing digital inclusion and equity. Social and Emotional Learning The conference will examine how social-emotional competencies contribute to sustainability by promoting empathy, collaboration, resilience, and responsible decision-making. Inclusive and Equitable Education Sessions will emphasize ensuring that education reaches learners from all backgrounds and promotes equal opportunities. Global Partnerships The event will encourage stronger collaboration among governments, educational institutions, civil society organizations, and the private sector. Who Can Submit Proposals? UNESCO welcomes proposals from a broad range of Education for Sustainable Development stakeholders. Eligible organizations include: United Nations agencies Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Academic institutions Universities and research centers Private sector organizations Government institutions UNESCO Member States International organizations Regional organizations Educational institutions NGOs Multi-stakeholder partnerships Organizations from every region of the world are encouraged to participate. About the Parallel Sessions Selected organizations will co-organize thematic parallel sessions lasting up to 90 minutes . These sessions should: Encourage dialogue. Promote knowledge exchange. Share innovative practices. Present research findings. Highlight practical experiences. Foster collaboration among stakeholders. The sessions are intended to complement the conference s plenary discussions and contribute directly to the implementation of Education for Sustainable Development worldwide. Proposal Submission Process Organizations interested in participating should follow these steps: Develop a proposal for a thematic parallel session. Ensure the session does not exceed 90 minutes. Complete the official proposal questionnaire. Follow all instructions provided in the questionnaire. Submit the proposal before the application deadline. Coordinating presentations. Facilitating the session during the conference in Nairobi. title: Global Youth Climate Training Programme 2026: Fully Online Free Climate Policy & Advocacy Training for Young People Worldwide – How to Apply, Eligibility, Benefits, Timeline, and Deadline
summary: The Global Youth Climate Training Programme (GYCT) 2026 is now accepting applications from young people around the world who are passionate about climate action, environmental sustainability, and international climate policy. Designed as a free, fully online capacity-development programme, GYCT provides participants with an opportunity to deepen their understanding of global climate governance, international negotiations, and practical climate advocacy while learning directly from experienced experts and climate negotiators. As climate change continues to shape the future of every country, empowering young people with the knowledge and skills to participate meaningfully in climate discussions has become increasingly important. The Global Youth Climate Training Programme serves as a gateway for emerging climate leaders who want to contribute to national, regional, and international climate initiatives. Whether you are already involved in climate activism or are just beginning your journey into environmental advocacy, this programme offers valuable learning opportunities that can strengthen your ability to engage in climate-related decision-making and policy discussions. What is the Global Youth Climate Training Programme (GYCT)? The Global Youth Climate Training Programme (GYCT) is an international online learning initiative that equips young people with essential knowledge about international climate policy, climate negotiations, and practical advocacy skills. The programme is designed to ensure that participants understand how international climate agreements are negotiated and implemented while also developing the confidence to advocate effectively for climate solutions within their communities and beyond. Unlike many climate education programmes that require travel or expensive participation fees, GYCT is completely free and delivered entirely online, making it accessible to participants from around the world. The programme also reflects a commitment to inclusivity by providing closed captions during sessions and offering live interpretation in selected languages for the main training sessions. Why You Should Apply Climate change remains one of the world s most pressing challenges, and young people continue to play a significant role in shaping climate action across local and global platforms. Participating in GYCT can help you: Build a strong understanding of international climate policy. Learn how global climate negotiations operate. Develop practical climate advocacy skills. Gain insights from experienced climate experts. Network with young climate leaders worldwide. Improve your understanding of the United Nations climate process. Prepare for future participation in climate conferences and advocacy initiatives. Become better equipped to contribute to environmental policy discussions in your country. Programme Structure The 2026 edition has been carefully designed to combine expert-led learning with more specialized mentorship opportunities. Phase One: Four Expert-Led Sessions The main programme consists of four online expert-led sessions scheduled to take place between: 2 September 2026 – 22 September 2026 These sessions will: Be conducted online. Be delivered in English. Include closed captions. Offer selected live interpretation services, including Spanish. Be recorded and later released publicly. These sessions are open to programme participants and focus on strengthening participants knowledge of climate governance, policy, and advocacy. Phase Two: Advanced Negotiator Alumni Pathway Following the main programme, 20 selected participants will be invited to join an exclusive learning pathway facilitated by Global Youth Coalition (GYC) and Youth Negotiators Academy (YNA) negotiator alumni. These additional sessions will run between: 29 September 2026 – 13 October 2026 The advanced pathway includes: Three additional online sessions. Instruction in English. Closed captions. No live interpretation. Sessions will not be recorded. Because only 20 participants will be selected, this component provides a more personalized learning experience with experienced climate negotiators. Learning Experience Participants can expect an engaging and interactive learning environment that emphasizes both theory and practice. Throughout the programme, learners will: Explore international climate agreements. Understand global climate governance. Learn practical advocacy techniques. Gain knowledge from leading experts. Discuss current climate challenges. Engage with fellow young climate advocates from different countries. Build skills useful for future climate leadership opportunities. Language Accessibility GYCT seeks to make learning accessible to a global audience. Main Sessions Participants will benefit from: English instruction Closed captions Live interpretation in selected languages Spanish interpretation Public recordings after the sessions Additional Sessions Selected participants joining the alumni pathway will receive: English instruction Closed captions No live interpretation No recordings Opportunity to Stay at the GYC House During COP31 An exciting feature of the programme is that GYCT participants will have the opportunity to apply to stay at the GYC House in Antalya during COP31 . This presents an additional opportunity for participants interested in engaging more closely with international climate events and networking with fellow youth climate leaders. However, acceptance into the training programme does not automatically guarantee accommodation. Financial Support The programme is offered completely free of charge. title: Council of Europe World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation 2026 in Strasbourg, France: Fully Funded Opportunity for Young Democracy Leaders Worldwide
summary: Applications are now open for the Council of Europe World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation 2026, an international opportunity that will bring up to 50 young people to Strasbourg, France, to participate in one of the Council of Europe’s major platforms for dialogue on democracy, democratic innovation, youth participation, and the future of democratic societies. The youth delegation will participate in the 14th edition of the World Forum for Democracy, scheduled to take place in Strasbourg on 2–3 November 2026 under the theme “Rupture or Renewal? Democratic Security for Our Future.” The Forum will take place within the framework of the New Democratic Pact for Europe, an initiative developed by the Council of Europe in response to emerging challenges facing European democracies. Selected youth delegates will have a broader programme than attendance at the main Forum alone. They will arrive in Strasbourg on 30 October 2026 and participate in dedicated pre-event training on 31 October and 1 November. They will then attend the World Forum for Democracy on 2–3 November and participate in the dedicated Youth Day on 4 November before departing Strasbourg on 5 November 2026. The opportunity is particularly attractive because the Council of Europe will cover travel and visa costs in accordance with its applicable rules, while accommodation and meals will be provided at the European Youth Centre Strasbourg. Applications are open to young people aged 18–30 who represent youth organisations and/or youth movements working on democracy, youth participation, or innovative democratic practices at local, regional, national, or international level. The application deadline is 14 August 2026 at 14:00 Strasbourg time. About the World Forum for Democracy 2026 The World Forum for Democracy is a platform created to bring together political decision-makers, civil society activists, youth representatives, practitioners, and other stakeholders to discuss solutions to major challenges facing democracies around the world. Rather than focusing exclusively on theoretical discussions about democracy, the Forum examines experimental initiatives, emerging practices, and innovative approaches that can strengthen democratic societies. It provides a space where participants can explore how grassroots democratic innovations might be transferred or expanded to the systemic level. Through this approach, the World Forum for Democracy contributes to efforts to make democratic structures and institutions more: Participatory Inclusive Responsive Innovative Resilient The 2026 edition will be the 14th World Forum for Democracy. World Forum for Democracy 2026 Theme The 14th edition of the World Forum for Democracy will take place under the title: “Rupture or Renewal? Democratic Security for Our Future” The Forum will be organized within the framework of the New Democratic Pact for Europe. The theme reflects ongoing discussions about the future of democracy and the need to ensure democratic systems are prepared to respond to new and evolving challenges. Understanding the New Democratic Pact for Europe The New Democratic Pact for Europe represents the Council of Europe’s response to contemporary challenges facing democratic societies. The initiative is firmly focused on the future and provides a framework for considering how European democracies can prepare for emerging political, social, institutional, and democratic challenges. The Council of Europe’s member states have supported the Pact since 2025. Over a period of two years, the Council of Europe has conducted broad consultations involving stakeholders such as: Member states Regions Territories Civil society Universities These consultations seek to contribute to a stronger understanding of the future of democracy in Europe and how democratic institutions can prepare for emerging challenges. The World Forum for Democracy 2026 will contribute to this broader process. About the World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation Youth participation is an important component of the World Forum for Democracy. For the 2026 edition, the Council of Europe is recruiting a dedicated youth delegation consisting of up to 50 participants. The delegation will bring youth perspectives into discussions concerning the New Democratic Pact for Europe and the broader future of democratic societies. The Council of Europe intends to select a diverse group of young people capable of offering different experiences, ideas, and perspectives on democracy. Particular relevance is given to young people who are already involved in finding solutions and developing ideas capable of strengthening or revitalizing democratic systems, especially where those systems may be at risk. Number of Participants The youth delegation will include: Up to 50 participants. The selection aims to create a group reflecting the diversity of young people around the world while bringing together different perspectives and experiences relating to democracy. What Selected Youth Delegates Will Do Selected participants will engage in several stages of the programme. These include: Online preparations Arrival in Strasbourg Pre-event youth delegation training Participation in the World Forum for Democracy Participation in Youth Day Follow-up within their organisations and communities Stage 1: Online Preparations The programme begins before participants travel to France. Online preparations are scheduled for: September–October 2026. Selected delegates must be available to participate in these preparatory activities. The online component forms part of the overall activity, meaning applicants should consider their availability for the entire programme rather than only the physical event in Strasbourg. Stage 2: Arrival in Strasbourg Selected youth delegates are expected to arrive in: Strasbourg, France, on 30 October 2026. This will allow participants to begin the in-person component before the main World Forum for Democracy. Stage 3: Pre-Event Training for the Youth Delegation A dedicated training programme for youth delegates will take place on: 31 October–1 November 2026. This two-day training takes place immediately before the World Forum for Democracy. The dedicated preparation provides the youth delegation with an opportunity to prepare for meaningful participation in the Forum and engage with the themes being discussed. Stage 4: World Forum for Democracy The main World Forum for Democracy takes place on: 2–3 November 2026. Youth delegates will participate alongside other stakeholders involved in discussions about democratic challenges, innovations, and the future of democratic security. The Forum creates a platform where political decision-makers and activists can discuss possible responses to challenges affecting democracies worldwide. Stage 5: World Forum for Democracy Youth Day Following the main Forum, the youth delegation will participate in a dedicated Youth Day on: 4 November 2026. Youth Day provides an additional space for young participants to engage with the Forum’s themes and strengthen the youth perspective within discussions surrounding democracy and the New Democratic Pact for Europe. Stage 6: Departure Participants are scheduled to depart Strasbourg on: 5 November 2026. The full in-person period therefore runs from 30 October to 5 November 2026. Complete Programme Timeline Applicants should take careful note of the programme schedule because full participation is required. September–October 2026 Online preparations for selected youth delegates. 30 October 2026 Arrival in Strasbourg, France. 31 October–1 November 2026 Pre-event training for the youth delegation. 2–3 November 2026 Participation in the 14th World Forum for Democracy. 4 November 2026 Participation in Youth Day. 5 November 2026 Departure from Strasbourg. Who Can Apply? The World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation 2026 is intended for young people who are actively involved in democracy, youth participation, or innovative democratic practices. Candidates must satisfy the eligibility requirements established by the Council of Europe. Age Requirement Applicants must be: 18–30 years old. Candidates outside this age range do not meet the age profile stated in the official call. English Language Requirement Applicants must be able to work autonomously in English. This means participants should possess sufficient English-language ability to participate independently in: Preparatory activities Training Forum discussions Youth activities Group work Follow-up engagement The source does not state that applicants need to submit a formal English-language examination certificate. Organisational or Movement Representation Applicants should represent a: Youth organisation; and/or Youth movement The organisation or movement should be active at one or more of the following levels: Local Regional National International Its activities should relate to relevant areas such as: Democracy Youth participation Innovative democratic practices The call therefore seeks young people who are already connected to organisations, movements, initiatives, or networks contributing to democratic participation. Commitment to Democracy and Youth Participation Candidates should be engaged with issues relating to democracy and youth participation. The delegation is intended to include young people who can bring substantive experiences and perspectives to discussions concerning democratic systems and their future. This may be particularly relevant to applicants involved in developing ideas or solutions to strengthen democracy in places where democratic systems face challenges. Full Availability Is Required Applicants must be available for the entire programme. This includes: Online preparation during September–October 2026 Youth delegation training on 31 October–1 November 2026 World Forum for Democracy on 2–3 November 2026 Youth Day on 4 November 2026 Candidates should therefore verify their availability before submitting an application. Follow-Up Capacity Applicants must be in a position to follow up on the results of the World Forum for Democracy within their organisations and communities. Participation is therefore not intended to end when delegates leave Strasbourg. Successful applicants should be prepared to transfer knowledge, ideas, discussions, and lessons from the Forum into their own environments. Potential follow-up contexts could include their: Youth organisations Youth movements Communities Networks Local initiatives The specific format of follow-up activities is not detailed in the information provided. Previous Council of Europe Experience Previous involvement with the Council of Europe youth sector in democratic participation is considered an asset. This is particularly relevant for candidates who have participated in activities organized by: The Council of Europe Youth Department Youth Department partners European Youth Foundation grantees Previous involvement in initiatives contributing to the New Democratic Pact for Europe may also strengthen an applicant’s profile. However, the call describes previous involvement as an asset rather than stating it as a mandatory eligibility condition. What Does the World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation Cover? The Council of Europe provides substantial financial and logistical support for selected participants. Travel Costs All travel costs are covered by the Council of Europe in accordance with its applicable rules. This substantially reduces the financial barrier for selected young people travelling to Strasbourg. Visa Costs Visa costs are also covered by the Council of Europe in accordance with its rules. This is particularly relevant to participants who require a visa to enter France. Applicants who require visas should nevertheless be prepared to complete all required visa procedures and provide any necessary documentation within the relevant timelines. Accommodation Accommodation will be provided at the: European Youth Centre Strasbourg. Selected participants therefore do not need to arrange their own accommodation for the official programme period covered by the organisers. Meals Meals are also provided at the European Youth Centre Strasbourg. European Youth Centre Strasbourg The European Youth Centre Strasbourg will serve as the accommodation venue for selected youth delegates. The Centre forms part of the Council of Europe’s infrastructure supporting youth activities and provides a setting for international youth learning, training, dialogue, and cooperation. Having delegates accommodated within the European Youth Centre also supports interaction and networking among participants during the programme. Why Young Democracy Leaders Should Apply The World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation provides young people with an opportunity to contribute their perspectives to international discussions on democracy. Young people are not simply passive observers of democratic change. They participate in social movements, civil society organisations, community initiatives, political discussions, digital activism, youth organisations, and innovative democratic practices. The Youth Delegation provides a platform for some of these perspectives to enter discussions involving decision-makers, activists, and other democracy stakeholders. International Exposure Participation in an international forum in Strasbourg gives young delegates exposure to perspectives and experiences beyond their immediate communities. The delegation itself is intended to reflect the diversity of young people around the world. Participants can therefore engage with peers who may have very different experiences of: Democracy Civic participation Youth engagement Community organisation Democratic innovation Networking Opportunities Bringing together up to 50 youth representatives creates opportunities for international networking and peer learning. Participants can interact with other young leaders as well as stakeholders participating in the wider World Forum for Democracy. These connections may contribute to future: Youth collaborations Democracy initiatives Advocacy projects International partnerships Knowledge exchange Opportunity to Bring Youth Perspectives to International Discussions A central purpose of the youth delegation is to ensure that youth perspectives contribute to discussions about the New Democratic Pact for Europe. Young participants can bring experiences from their organisations and communities into conversations concerning democratic security and the future of democracy. Professional and Leadership Development The programme also provides a learning experience for young people engaged in democracy and youth participation. Participation in online preparation, dedicated training, international dialogue, and follow-up can strengthen competencies relevant to: Youth leadership Civic engagement Advocacy Intercultural communication Democratic participation International cooperation Community engagement Importance of Follow-Up After the Forum Applicants should pay particular attention to the requirement concerning follow-up. The Council of Europe is seeking participants who can take the Forum’s results back to their organisations and communities. A competitive applicant should therefore be able to demonstrate a meaningful connection to a youth organisation, movement, network, or community where lessons from the Forum can continue to generate value. When preparing an application, candidates may benefit from considering how they could share or apply what they learn after returning home. How to Apply Applications must be submitted online through the official application process provided by the Council of Europe Youth Department. Applicants should carefully review the concept note and official call for applications before completing the form. Before applying, candidates should ensure they can demonstrate: That they are between 18 and 30 years old. Their ability to work autonomously in English. Their involvement with a relevant youth organisation or movement. Their engagement with democracy, youth participation, or innovative democratic practices. Their availability for the full programme. Their ability to follow up on the Forum’s outcomes within their organisation or community. Any relevant previous involvement with the Council of Europe youth sector, where applicable. Click HERE to begin your application Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation 2026 is: 14 August 2026 at 14:00 Strasbourg time. Applicants should take particular note of the specified time zone and should not assume they can submit until the end of the day in their own country. Submitting well before the deadline is advisable to avoid last-minute technical problems. Selection Considerations The information provided does not give a detailed numerical scoring system for applications. However, the participant profile clearly indicates that candidates should demonstrate alignment with the programme’s objectives. Relevant factors include: Age eligibility Ability to work in English Active youth organisation or movement involvement Engagement in democracy and youth participation Full availability Ability to conduct follow-up activities Diversity of perspectives Relevant previous Council of Europe youth-sector engagement, where applicable Because the delegation will contain only up to 50 participants, applicants should present their experiences and motivations clearly and specifically. Practical Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Demonstrate Real Engagement With Democracy Rather than simply stating that you are interested in democracy, provide concrete examples of your involvement. This might include your work within a youth organisation, movement, civic initiative, community project, or another relevant activity. Explain Your Role Clearly Describe what you personally do within your organisation or movement. Applicants should distinguish their own contributions from the general achievements of the organisation they represent. Connect Your Experience to the Forum Show how your experiences relate to: Democracy Youth participation Democratic innovation Democratic security Inclusive participation The future of democratic institutions Demonstrate Follow-Up Potential Since participants must follow up on Forum results, explain how your organisation or community could benefit from your participation. A strong application should show that the opportunity will create value beyond the individual applicant. Confirm Your Availability Do not overlook the programme s time commitment. Selected delegates must participate in online preparation and the complete in-person programme in Strasbourg. Highlight Relevant Council of Europe Experience If you have previously participated in activities connected to the Council of Europe Youth Department, its partners, European Youth Foundation grantees, or initiatives connected to the New Democratic Pact for Europe, include this information where the application allows. Previous participation is considered an asset. Key Dates to Remember Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Application deadline: 14 August 2026 at 14:00 Strasbourg time Online preparations: September–October 2026 Arrival in Strasbourg: 30 October 2026 Youth delegation training: 31 October–1 November 2026 World Forum for Democracy: 2–3 November 2026 Youth Day: 4 November 2026 Departure from Strasbourg: 5 November 2026 For more information about the Council of Europe World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation 2026, visit HERE Conclusion The Council of Europe World Forum for Democracy Youth Delegation 2026 offers an important international opportunity for young people actively engaged in democracy, youth participation, and innovative democratic practices to contribute their perspectives to discussions about the future of democratic societies. Up to 50 young participants will be selected to join the delegation in Strasbourg, France. Their engagement will include online preparations during September and October, dedicated pre-event training, participation in the 14th World Forum for Democracy under the theme “Rupture or Renewal? Democratic Security for Our Future,” and a dedicated Youth Day. The opportunity is particularly accessible because the Council of Europe will cover travel and visa costs according to its rules, while accommodation and meals will be provided at the European Youth Centre Strasbourg. Applicants must be between 18 and 30 years old, be able to work autonomously in English, represent a youth organisation and/or youth movement working on relevant democratic issues, participate in the complete programme, and be capable of following up on the Forum s outcomes within their organisations and communities. With the application deadline set for 14 August 2026 at 14:00 Strasbourg time, eligible young democracy leaders should review the official call carefully, prepare strong applications demonstrating their practical involvement in democratic participation, and submit before the deadline.
